questions.question: Explain two ways good customer service can benefit a business.

points.text: Good customer service (1) builds customer loyalty - satisfied customers return and spend more over time (customer lifetime value), and (2) generates word-of-mouth recommendations - happy customers tell others, providing free credible advertising that is more trusted than paid marketing.

questions.question: Describe how a business can monitor the quality of its customer service.

points.text: Monitoring methods: (1) Customer feedback surveys (online, in-store, post-purchase) - quantitative data on satisfaction scores and qualitative comments. (2) Mystery shoppers - trained evaluators pose as customers and rate service against specific criteria (greeting, product knowledge, wait times). questions.question: Evaluate whether investing in customer service training is more important than investing in marketing.

points.text: Customer service training benefits: loyal customers who spend more over time, fewer complaints reducing costs, positive word-of-mouth reducing need for advertising, motivated staff who feel competent. Marketing benefits: reaches new customers, builds brand awareness, drives immediate sales. markScheme.exemplarAnswer: A grade 9 response will: analyse chatbots (24/7 availability, handles common queries instantly, low cost per interaction, consistent responses, but cannot handle complex/emotional issues, can frustrate customers with limited understanding); human advisors (empathy and judgement for complex issues, can de-escalate complaints, build relationships, but limited availability, higher cost, variable quality depending on training/mood); conclude: a hybrid approach is optimal - chatbots for routine queries (order tracking, returns policy, FAQs) freeing humans for complex and emotional interactions, giving customers the right support at the right time while controlling costs.
